findings.title: Default getThreads calls embed an all-null SLA filter that makes the SQL invalid
findings.failure: Every MCP getThreads call that leaves slaStatuses and slaTypes at their null defaults, including every existing caller, now sends serviceLevelAgreements as an object of nulls. threadsQuery parses that object and keeps it (ThreadsFilter defaults the missing updatedAt to null and does not collapse the object). getThreadsWithoutLabels passes it to threadDb.getThreads, which builds the WHERE via createFilters and buildFilters. The top-level serviceLevelAgreements builder returns an empty fragment when statuses, types, and updatedAt are all null. buildFilters still ANDs that fragment in, because the value is non-null and lodash compact only drops null. This operation also always sends createdAt, and rangeFilter turns a null/null range into `1 = 1`, so the clause is the empty fragment glued with AND to `1 = 1` (and to any real filters). slonik 45.5.0 sql.join emits the separator between every member, including a member whose SQL text is empty, so the query text contains `AND  AND` or a trailing `AND`. Postgres rejects it and the tool errors. Calls that set slaStatuses or slaTypes skip the empty return and emit a real EXISTS, so only the default path breaks. The public threads API is unchanged for clients that omit the field.
findings.fix: Make the all-null branch in the top-level builder return `sql.fragment`1 = 1`` (threadDbFilterUtils.ts around the serviceLevelAgreements callback that currently returns `sql.fragment``` `), the same way surveyResponse in that function and rangeFilter already do. The nested buildExistsBasedFilterSql branch already skips an all-null object; changing only that branch leaves getThreads broken. Alternatively, stop inlining the object and pass `$serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter = null` through as `serviceLevelAgreements: $serviceLevelAgreements`, matching surveyResponse in this same operation, so a null variable is omitted by buildFilters.
findings.evidence: getThreads.graphql always inlines serviceLevelAgreements: { statuses: $slaStatuses, types: $slaTypes } with both variables defaulting to null, next to createdAt: { after, before }. packages/core-graphql/src/threads/threadsFilter.ts:58-73 keeps that object and defaults updatedAt to null. packages/core-graphql/src/threads/threadsQuery.ts:216 calls getThreadsWithoutLabels, which calls threadDb.getThreads. packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-946 returns sql.fragment`` when all three inner fields are null; surveyResponse at 1156-1164 returns sql.fragment`1=1` for the same shape. The nested check at 647-649 no-ops and is not the path createFilters uses for the top-level filter (buildBaseFilterSql calls rdsDbUtils.filtering.buildFilters). packages/db/src/filtering.ts:114-125 ANDs every non-null builder result; lines 14-31 make an empty datetime range `1 = 1`. threadDb.ts:1252 interpolates that fragment as `AND ${filters} AND ${excludeTestThreadsFilter}`. packages/db/package.json pins slonik 45.5.0; sql.join places the glue between members even when a member's SQL is empty. Repo search for `serviceLevelAgreements: {` shows no other caller sends the all-null object; threadDbFilterUtils.test.ts only covers cases with a type, status, or updatedAt set.

checked_fine: Deploy: the diff is only three MCP operation documents. entrypoint.sh still fetches the live schema; ServiceLevelAgreementStatusSummary, the status union, and ServiceLevelAgreementFilter already exist. No migration, export, env var, or permission change. Apollo MCP startup validation should accept the operations.

getThreadDetails and searchThreads only add serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary. Every union member and its schema fields are selected (Pending and ImminentBreach include pausedAt and remainingMinutesAtPause; Breaching, Achieved, Breached, and Cancelled match the schema). Enum names match ServiceLevelAgreementStatus and ServiceLevelAgreementType in packages/models.

The summary resolver and dataloader are unchanged. Threads with both tierId and serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId null return all-null without a query. Other threads batch through getLatestServiceLevelAgreementTrackersByThreadIds, which matches idx_sla_trackers_workspace_thread_type_created_at (workspace_id, thread_id, type, created_at DESC).
thread:read is still the only permission on getThreads. The tracker loader is the same one the public Thread.serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary field already uses.

When slaStatuses or slaTypes is set, the builder emits one EXISTS and ANDs type and status on the same tracker row, including completed rows. That matches the new getThreads comment and the newest-per-target summary from DISTINCT ON created_at DESC. Null still means that dimension is ignored.

Empty slaStatuses or slaTypes arrays fail the existing minLength(1) check on ThreadsFilter, the same as statuses and the other list filters. Null is the ignore value, and these variables use the same `= null` default pattern as $statuses.
getMyAssignedThreads and getCustomerThreads are unchanged and still omit the summary. The PR only claims getThreadDetails, getThreads, and searchThreads.
Rollback of the MCP image restores the previous operations. No stored schema, retention, or migration change, so there is no one-way data door.

No dead code: the new selections and variables are inside the three operations Apollo MCP loads from services/mcp-server/operations (mcp.config.yaml paths: /data/operations/). Repo search shows no other reader of these operation files.
